newsitem.title: USA: Medarex to buy GenPharm for $65 mln stock.
newsitem.headline: Medarex to buy GenPharm for $65 mln stock.

text.p: Medarex Inc said on Tuesday it signed a definitive agreement to acquire GenPharm International Inc, a privately-held biopharmaceutical company, for up to $65 milllion in Medarex common stock.

Medarex said the acquisition would expand its business and technology base to include GenPharm's patented HuMab-Mouse, an antibody discovery platform which complemented Medarex's Bispecific antibody technology.

The company said it expected to receive $33 million in cash by the end of 1998 through a combination of GenPharm's cash on hand and certain patent licence fees and related payments from third parties.
It would also obtain three new corporate partnerships with Eisai Co Ltd, Centocor Inc and LeukoSite Inc, the company said.

The deal was expected to close in the third quarter 1997. Medarex said it would issue stock worth up to $65 million, or up to 3.5 million shares, in 1997 after GenPharm shareholder approval and the meeting of certain regulatory requirements.
Medarex said it would issue additional shares by the end of 1998 for the rest of the purchase price but only if GenPharm received certain patent license fees and related payments.
GenPharm's HuMab-Mouse could be used to generate human monoclonal antibodies with strong binding abilities to a wide variety of disease targets, Medarex said.
